title: Recorded chronolexogram v0.3.0
description: A fact as a cell records it: at recorded_at, recording_actor recorded that this event took place with these fields, on this legal basis, and that it legally applies or took place at effective_at (paper P:46: two times). A gram is only ever appended, never edited; a correction is a new gram. A field that was not filled in is present as null: the gram keeps the shape of the stream. Since v0.2.0 a gram has its own id (uuid v7, assigned by the cell) and refers, with a name from the law, to the gram it belongs to (refers_to); there is no case or decision identifier anymore. Groups follow from those references: the root of a gram is the root of the gram it refers to.

id.description: The gram's own id: a uuid (v7, increasing over time) that the cell assigns on recording, under the same lock as recorded_at. A chronicle from before v0.2.0 is not converted.

type.description: Open vocabulary (RFC-022 sec. 1), for example executogram or submission.

subtype.description: The subtype within the type, for example aanvraag for a submission.

stage.description: From the law or the stream: the stage (RFC-008), for a stage decretogram, a submission (AANVRAAG) or an act (BEKENDMAKING).

legal_character.description: Only for a decision the cell itself made: the legal character from the article's produces (RFC-008), for example BESCHIKKING.

decision_type.description: Only for a decision: the kind of decision from produces, for example TOEKENNING.

regulation.description: Only for a decision: the regulation it rests on.

regulation_valid_from.description: Only for a decision: the date from which that version of the regulation applies.

competent_authority.description: Only for a decision, and only if the regulation names a competent authority: that authority. The process checks it against the authority it acts for (on_behalf_of) and its mandates, and records nothing for a different authority; if the regulation names none, this field is absent and the process issues a warning.

acting_actor.description: Only for a decision a process made: who acted. Alongside recording_actor (who records) and competent_authority (who the law empowers), the third axis of RFC-022 sec. 2. The channel is simulated: the identity is what the user entered.

legal_basis.description: The legal basis of the role, if the process configuration names one.

on_behalf_of.description: The authority on whose behalf the action was taken.

mandate.description: The legal basis of the mandate (Awb 10:1), if that authority is not the process's own authority.

effective_at.description: The moment at which the fact legally applies or took place (RFC 3339, with time zone). Defaults to recorded_at; an event can bind it to a submitted value (see effective_at_legal_basis), and in an initial state it is set by hand, such as the date of a decision.

effective_at_legal_basis.description: If the event bound effective_at to a submitted value and that value was present: why that moment legally counts, from the law. For example the day of receipt of an application that arrived by another route (Awb 4:13, with the policy for paper applications). Since v0.3.0 also without a submitted value, if the law says why the moment of recording counts (a portal application is received when the portal records it).

recorded_at.description: The moment at which the cell recorded the gram: always its own clock, for an initial state the load time. Required: a chronicle with a gram that lacks it is refused when loaded.

refers_to.description: Which grams this gram refers to, per name from the law text (on_application, application, decision, amends, concerns). The names, and what each may point to, are given by the establishing article (produces.extensions.chronolex.establishes[].refers_to) or the stream; on recording, the cell checks that the gram exists and matches. No reference: the gram is itself a root.

stream.description: The stream definition the gram was built with, with the hash of that file.

provenance.description: Only if the gram was not established by the cell itself. initial_state: placed into an empty chronicle on startup, not computed (no engine trace).

field_provenance.description: Since v0.3.0: per field that the receiving channel could supply ($supplied in the stream), where its value came from this time. The same field can come from a register one time (the portal filled it in beforehand, from a register the policy names) and from the applicant another time (the register does not know it). The law decides that the field is in the gram (such as Wpp 102 lid 3: the statutory name); the provenance says only where the value came from.

source.description: channel: the login or the route supplied it; register: the portal queried a register the policy names; applicant or handler: whoever submitted typed it in.

legal_basis.description: Why that source may supply the field: the rule of the channel or the policy that names the register.

inputs.description: Only for an action a process computed (a decision, a follow-up, or a fact from the course of the case): for each parameter that took part, the value and its provenance (RFC-013 accepted_values). None of this is a fact of the cell itself; it is included so the decision can be traced.

receipt.description: Only for an action a process computed: what took part, so it can be repeated (RFC-013 execution receipt, RFC-022 sec. 1.3 for the streams).
